landmarks.name: Cape Coast Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic fortress used in the trans-Atlantic slave trade, now a museum and UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: Cape Coast Castle is one of about forty "slave castles", or large commercial forts, built on the Gold Coast of West Africa by European traders. Cape Coast Castle is located in the Central Region of Ghana. It was originally a Portuguese "feitoria" or trading post, established in 1555, which was named Cabo Corso, meaning "Short Cape."

landmarks.name: Kakum National Park
landmarks.writeup: A tropical rainforest reserve known for its canopy walkway and diverse wildlife.

wiki.extract: Kakum National Park, located in the coastal environs of the Central Region of Ghana, covers an area of 375 square kilometres (145 sq mi). Established in 1931 as a reserve, it was gazetted as a national park only in 1992 after an initial survey of avifauna was conducted. The area is covered with tropical forest. The uniqueness of this park lies in the fact that it was established at the initiative of the local people and not by the State Department of wildlife who are responsible for wildlife preservation in Ghana. It is one of only 3 locations in Africa with a canopy walkway, which is 350 metres (1,150 ft) long and connects seven tree tops which provides access to the forest.

landmarks.name: Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum
landmarks.writeup: Memorial park dedicated to Ghana's first president and prominent independence leader.

wiki.extract: The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and Mausoleum is located in downtown Accra, the capital of Ghana.

cultural_events.name: Homowo Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated by the Ga people to mark the end of a historic famine with feasting and rituals.

cultural_events.name: Panafest
cultural_events.writeup: A cultural festival promoting Pan-Africanism and African heritage through music, dance, and art.

food_writeup: Ghanaian cuisine features staples like jollof rice, fufu, banku, and dishes rich in spices and palm oil, reflecting diverse ethnic traditions.
brief_history: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule in 1957, led by Kwame Nkrumah. It has a history of powerful kingdoms and was a major center in the trans-Atlantic slave trade.
current_conflicts: Ghana is generally stable with no significant internal conflicts; however, there are occasional disputes over land and natural resources.
